Direct Empirical Scaling Fit With GSE164378 3’ CITE-seq

This tutorial runs the direct empirical scaling workflow on the same GSE164378 3’ CITE-seq RNA-ADT example used by the Gaussian spike tutorials. Here we do not fit the spike model. We sample a grid of cell numbers and UMI depths, compute fixed-rank empirical RNA-ADT mutual information, and fit the empirical scaling law directly.

library(scScale)
## Loading required package: Matrix
data(gse164378_3p_citeseq_hvg)

rna_counts <- gse164378_3p_citeseq_hvg$rna_counts
adt_counts <- gse164378_3p_citeseq_hvg$adt_counts
count_transform <- "log1p_cpm"

sampling_rates <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.70, 0.85, 1.00)
n_grid <- c(500, 1000, 2000, 4000)
r_empirical <- 12

Fit Empirical Scaling Law

scscale_empirical_scaling_fit() samples the grid, preprocesses each sampled matrix in the standard way, computes empirical subspace MI, and fits the cell-number, UMI, and joint laws into one object.

fit <- scscale_empirical_scaling_fit(
  rna_counts,
  adt_counts,
  n_grid = n_grid,
  sampling_rates = sampling_rates,
  r = r_empirical,
  n_replicates = 1,
  n_ref = max(n_grid),
  U_ref = max(sampling_rates) * stats::median(Matrix::colSums(rna_counts)),
  joint_mode = "hybrid",
  seed = 164378,
  count_transform = count_transform
)

fit
## scScale direct empirical I(n,U) fit
##   grid rows: 28
##   rank: 12  replicates: 1
##   reference: n_ref=4000, U_ref=5692.5
##   joint mode: hybrid
##   I_infinity: 6.073
##   joint rmse: 0.066966
##   ceiling diagnostics:
##   from_cell_marginal    from_umi_marginal              average 
##             6.051200             6.028000             6.039600 
##            joint_fit max_abs_gap_to_joint 
##             6.073000             0.045081

The fitted joint law uses one global parameter set across the sampled grid.

data.frame(
  parameter = names(c(fit$joint_fit$coefficients, fit$joint_fit$fixed)),
  value = as.numeric(c(fit$joint_fit$coefficients, fit$joint_fit$fixed)),
  row.names = NULL
)
##    parameter        value
## 1 I_infinity 6.073049e+00
## 2        C_n 2.983183e+06
## 3        C_U 1.273953e+01
## 4        A_n 6.330869e-05
## 5        A_U 1.363946e+02
## 6   U_offset 2.823993e+02
fit$ceiling
##   from_cell_marginal    from_umi_marginal              average 
##           6.05115607           6.02796785           6.03956196 
##            joint_fit max_abs_gap_to_joint 
##           6.07304885           0.04508099
grid <- fit$grid
grid$sampling_rate_label <- factor(
  grid$sampling_rate,
  levels = sampling_rates,
  labels = paste0("rho = ", sampling_rates)
)

rho_to_U <- aggregate(U ~ sampling_rate, data = grid, FUN = unique)
rho_to_U <- rho_to_U[order(rho_to_U$sampling_rate), ]
rho_cols <- setNames(
  c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#56B4E9", "#E69F00", "#000000"),
  as.character(rho_to_U$sampling_rate)
)

Cell-Number Scaling

The cell-number marginal fit uses the full-depth grid slice.

cell_obs <- subset(grid, abs(U - fit$reference$U_ref) < 1e-8)
cell_obs <- cell_obs[order(cell_obs$n), ]

n_curve <- seq(min(n_grid), max(n_grid), length.out = 200)
cell_curve <- data.frame(n = n_curve)
cell_curve$I_fit <- predict(fit$cell_fit, cell_curve)

plot(
  cell_obs$n,
  cell_obs$I_empirical,
  pch = 16,
  col = "#0072B2",
  xlab = "Cell number n",
  ylab = expression(hat(I)(n~"|"~U[ref])),
  main = "Empirical cell-number scaling"
)
lines(cell_curve$n, cell_curve$I_fit, col = "#D55E00", lwd = 2)
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("empirical MI", "empirical fit"),
  col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"),
  pch = c(16, NA),
  lwd = c(NA, 2),
  bty = "n"
)

UMI Scaling

The UMI marginal fit uses the full-cell grid slice.

umi_obs <- subset(grid, n == fit$reference$n_ref)
umi_obs <- umi_obs[order(umi_obs$sampling_rate), ]

rho_curve <- seq(min(sampling_rates), max(sampling_rates), length.out = 200)
U_curve <- rho_curve * stats::median(Matrix::colSums(rna_counts))
umi_curve <- data.frame(U = U_curve, sampling_rate = rho_curve)
umi_curve$I_fit <- predict(fit$umi_fit, umi_curve)

plot(
  umi_obs$sampling_rate,
  umi_obs$I_empirical,
  pch = 16,
  col = "#0072B2",
  xlab = expression("Sampling rate " * rho),
  ylab = expression(hat(I)(U~"|"~n[ref])),
  main = "Empirical UMI scaling"
)
lines(umi_curve$sampling_rate, umi_curve$I_fit, col = "#D55E00", lwd = 2)
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("empirical MI", "empirical fit"),
  col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"),
  pch = c(16, NA),
  lwd = c(NA, 2),
  bty = "n"
)

Joint Scaling By UMI Level

The joint fit uses all grid points and one global parameter set. Each line below is the fitted cell-number scaling curve at one UMI sampling rate.

plot(
  NA,
  xlim = range(n_grid),
  ylim = range(c(grid$I_empirical, fit$fitted), na.rm = TRUE),
  xlab = "Cell number n",
  ylab = expression(hat(I)(n,U)),
  main = "Empirical joint scaling by UMI level"
)

for (rho in sampling_rates) {
  U_i <- rho_to_U$U[rho_to_U$sampling_rate == rho]
  obs_i <- grid[grid$sampling_rate == rho, ]
  obs_i <- obs_i[order(obs_i$n), ]
  points(obs_i$n, obs_i$I_empirical, pch = 16, col = rho_cols[as.character(rho)])
  pred_i <- data.frame(n = seq(min(n_grid), max(n_grid), length.out = 200), U = U_i)
  pred_i$I_fit <- predict(fit, pred_i)
  lines(pred_i$n, pred_i$I_fit, col = rho_cols[as.character(rho)], lwd = 2)
}

legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = paste0("rho = ", sampling_rates),
  col = rho_cols[as.character(sampling_rates)],
  pch = 16,
  lwd = 2,
  bty = "n",
  cex = 0.85
)

Grid and Residuals

grid_out <- grid
grid_out$I_fit <- fit$fitted
grid_out$residual <- fit$residuals
grid_out[, c("n", "sampling_rate", "U", "I_empirical", "I_fit", "residual", "r_eff")]

plot(
  grid_out$I_fit,
  grid_out$residual,
  pch = 16,
  col = rho_cols[as.character(grid_out$sampling_rate)],
  xlab = "Fitted I(n,U)",
  ylab = "Residual",
  main = "Joint empirical fit residuals"
)
abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
legend(
  "topright",
  legend = paste0("rho = ", sampling_rates),
  col = rho_cols[as.character(sampling_rates)],
  pch = 16,
